extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and investigators/applicants preparing P01 (Program Project) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer review of NIH P01 Program Project grants describing how to evaluate each subproject, core units, and the integrated program as a whole, including scoring conventions and common strengths/weaknesses to look for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five standard review criteria used to evaluate each subproject of a P01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to each individual subproject. Each subproject is reviewed using the five criteria (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) and receives an overall impact score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five standard review criteria used to evaluate each subproject of a P01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to each individual subproject. Consider qualifications and roles of PIs and key personnel. Each subproject receives an overall impact score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five standard review criteria used to evaluate each subproject of a P01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to each individual subproject. Innovation may not be required in all categories for major impact (see General Evaluation Principle). Each subproject receives an overall impact score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five standard review criteria used to evaluate each subproject of a P01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to each individual subproject. Reviewers assess the rigor and suitability of methods and plans. Each subproject receives an overall impact score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the five standard review criteria used to evaluate each subproject of a P01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to each individual subproject. Consider institutional support, facilities, and other resources. Each subproject receives an overall impact score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Individual Core Units
rubrics_metrics.description: Cores are evaluated on whether they are essential and justified for the proposed research, have the capability to fulfill the proposed function, and service two or more Projects (typically required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cores are not numerically scored; they are rated as "Recommended" or "Not Recommended." Common core types include Administrative, Biostatistics, Imaging, Genomics, Animal, Clinical, and Data Management cores. Reviewers should judge cost justification and degree to which cores provide unique value to multiple projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level integration and overall impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of the P01 as an integrated whole: assess whether the Program is scientifically compelling and whether individual Projects and Cores coordinate/synergize toward central objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers ask: Is the Program as a whole scientifically compelling? Is there coordination and synergy of individual research Projects and Cores toward the central objectives? Does the program leverage the cores effectively and create value beyond what individual projects could achieve separately? The overall P01 receives an Overall Impact Score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy (what reviewers look for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that Projects genuinely depend on each other and that Cores provide unique value, with coordinated leadership and shared resources that would not otherwise exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for genuine interdependence among projects (not merely parallel R01s), cores that provide unique services, coordinated leadership, and shared resources that add collective value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination (what reviewers look for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational and leadership mechanisms that enable the multi-project program to function coherently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicators include strong overall PI leadership, regular meetings/communication structure, internal advisory committee, external advisory committee, and annual planning processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Mass (what reviewers look for)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sufficient scale and capacity of the investigator team and institutional support to justify a program project approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for multiple investigators of high caliber, an established history of collaboration, clear institutional commitment, and resources beyond what individual grants would provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common P01 Weaknesses (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequently observed deficiencies that reduce the likelihood that a P01 is appropriate or competitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes lack of true synergy (projects function as parallel R01s), cores that don't justify their cost or are not integrated into projects, a single project that dominates the program (not truly multi-project), weak overall PI leadership, and insufficient internal coordination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: P01 Strategic Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical program-level expectations that affect whether a P01 is the right mechanism and how to plan one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant institutional commitment is typically required; multi-year planning (often 5+ years lead time); investigators must have demonstrated track record together; P01s are often used to renew or expand existing collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variations Across Institutes / FOA-specific emphases
rubrics_metrics.description: Different NIH institutes may emphasize different program elements or add additional criteria in funding announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NCI P01s often emphasize translational components; NIA emphasizes aging-relevant integration; NICHD emphasizes child health applications; NHLBI often includes clinical components. Reviewers and applicants should consult institute-specific announcements for additional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring conventions and ratings summary
rubrics_metrics.description: How numerical and categorical ratings are applied across components of the P01 review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each subproject receives an overall impact score on the 1–9 scale. The integrated P01 also receives an Overall Impact Score (1–9). Cores are not numerically scored but are judged "Recommended" or "Not Recommended."
